note: All resolutions derived by resampling from the same 1-min dataset

15min.note: Ring borderline at train, lost at test (likely short training window)

30min.note: Ring holds in test. Negative sign = UMAP ring orientation inverted vs 1h. |r|=0.303 comparable to 1h result.

conclusions.resolution_threshold: S1 ring forms at 15-min resolution and coarser. Finer resolution (1-min, 5-min) shows ring_cv > 0.40 — no ring.
conclusions.mechanism: At sub-15min, market microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce, individual trades) dominates over cycle dynamics. The vol_20 window (20 bars) captures only 20-minutes of volatility at 1-min resolution, too short to represent regime cycles.
conclusions.signal_quality: |r_OOS| is comparable across resolutions (0.29-0.32) once the ring forms. The signal amplitude is resolution-independent once above the threshold.
conclusions.sign_inversion: The 30-min result shows negative r_OOS (-0.303). This is a UMAP orientation artifact: the ring can be fit clockwise or counterclockwise randomly. Using both sin_theta and cos_theta as features (as in build_feature_vector) is immune to this.
conclusions.data_limitation: The 1-min dataset spans only 64 days. The 15/30-min resampled results have very short test windows (12-25 days). Statistical significance is lower than the 1h result (2 years test).
conclusions.verdict: PARTIAL PASS — ring threshold confirmed at ~15min. Signal strength (|r|~0.30) confirmed multi-timeframe. 1-min specific result = WEAK (r=0.055, no ring). Need longer sub-hourly data for definitive validation.
conclusions.recommendation: Use 15-min or 30-min for sub-hourly signal generation. Do NOT use 1-min or 5-min with current compact feature set.
